newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks tumble, while the dollar retreats.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks tumble, while the dollar retreats.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average raced lower on Wednesday as investors took profits after the blue-chip market failed for the second straight day to punch through the 8,000-point mark.
A strong performance by technology stocks lifted the Nasdaq Composite index to another record high, while the dollar retreated from a 3-1/2-year high against the German mark.
The Dow ended down 119.88 points, or 1.51 percent, at 7,842.43. An early rally stalled at 7,991.26.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,710 to 1,141 on heavy volume of 589 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

With the Dow unable to rally through the magic 8,000 level, investors began to take profits in earnest, and the afternoon was marked by a wave of sell programmes that briefly dragged the Dow below 7,800.
"It might have registered in some people's consciousness that 8,000 was pretty high," said Charles Pradilla, an analyst at Cowen & Co.
"This was just a bit of a big cap correction," he said. "We had a very, very big move, a lot of these stocks had gotten overvalued and now some money is coming out."
Analysts said the blue-chip market may pause in the near term but it appears to have enough backing to rally the Dow through the 8,000 mark.

"I expect it to hesitate a bit, see some psychological resistance at 8,000, but I think the ingredients are in place to overcome it short term," said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at Everen Securities Inc.
While the 30-stock Dow was under the gun after its recent jump into record territory, investors sought opportunities beyond the blue-chip arena.
Technology stocks attracted buyers, which lifted the Nasdaq index 1.53 points to 1,486.63, its fifth consecutive closing record high.
The dollar eased against the Japanese yen Wednesday after Japan said its trade surplus more than doubled in May, heightening concern about rising exports to the United States.
The dollar also retreated against the mark -- after extending its recent rally to a new 3-1/2-year high -- with a selloff on Wall Street eroding support late in the day.
The dollar ended at 112.75 yen, down from 112.85 at Tuesday's close and at 1.7605 marks, off from 1.7612.
The 30-year Treasury rose 7/32, or $2.19 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield to 6.56 percent from 6.59 percent Tuesday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
In commodity markets, soybean prices rose sharply for the second consecutive day on talk that prices had fallen far enough in recent weeks to spur demand from overseas buyers.
Soybeans for July delivery at the Chicago Board of Trade closed up 21 cents a bushel at $7.89.

At the New York Mercantile Exchange, oil prices ended lower after weekly oil industry data showed plentiful supplies and Iraq took another step toward resuming oil sales under a deal with the United Nations.
Crude oil for August delivery closed 27 cents a barrel lower at $19.46.
In overseas markets, London's FTSE 100 closed at 4,762.4, up 3.9 points, or 0.08 percent. The Tokyo exchange's 225-share Nikkei average closed at 19,697.17, down 156.72 points, or 0.79 percent.
